actions.heading: Actions
actions.issue: Issue a certificate with this CA
actions.delete.confirm: Yes, move it to the trash
actions.delete.warn.key: The key goes to the trash. Certificates and requests that use it show no key until it is restored. Its private key stays encrypted in the database until the trash is emptied.
actions.delete.warn.cert: The certificate goes to the trash. Certificates it issued are linked to another issuer if one exists; its revocation entries are kept and come back with it.
actions.delete.warn.request: The certificate signing request goes to the trash.
actions.delete.warn.crl: The revocation list goes to the trash.
actions.delete.warn.template: The template goes to the trash.
item.error.noname: The internal name must not be empty.
item.error.extract: The public key could not be extracted; it may already be in the database.
item.error.keypass: This action needs the key's own password.
item.error.torequest: The request could not be created. Details are in the server log.
keypw.heading: Key password
keypw.help: A key with its own password asks for it every time it is used. Resetting protects it with the database password again.
keypw.error.mismatch: The new passwords do not match or are empty.
keypw.error.current: The current key password is wrong.
dbpw.title: Database password
dbpw.heading: Change the database password
dbpw.intro: Changing the password, or the cost of deriving the key from it, also replaces the key that encrypts the private keys: every key protected by the database password is re-encrypted. A backup is saved first. Other sessions on this database are closed.
dbpw.background: go-ca keeps this database open in the background with the password from its configuration file, so the password cannot be changed here. To change it, remove the password from the database's section in the configuration file and restart go-ca, change it here, then put the new password into the configuration file and restart go-ca again.
dbpw.error.mismatch: The new passwords do not match.
newkey.title: New key
newkey.heading: New key
newkey.help: RSA keys of 4096 bits or more take a few seconds. Keys for key agreement or encapsulation cannot sign: they get their certificate from a CA. DSA keys cannot be generated by go-ca.
newkey.error.input: Enter a name and choose a key type.
keypick.note.p256: Small and fast; the default for TLS and CAs.
keypick.note.ed25519: The default for SSH and OpenPGP.
keypick.works.ed25519: OpenSSH, GnuPG, OpenSSL; few TLS clients
keypick.note.rsa3072: For old devices and mail clients without elliptic curves.
keypick.draft.warn: Draft standard: the encoding may still change, and keys or certificates made now may not be readable by later versions.

keypick.hidden.other: %d post-quantum and special key types are shown with expert fields.

purpose.title: New
purpose.heading: What do you want to create?
purpose.intro: Pick the purpose. go-ca chooses the key type, lifetime and extensions; you can change them before creating.
purpose.carry: The CA or request you came from is preselected in the form.
purpose.template.help: Opens the full editor with this template.
profile.root-ca.help: The top of a new hierarchy. Keep it offline; it signs intermediate CAs.
profile.root-ca.heading: Root CA
profile.intermediate-ca.help: Signed by one of your CAs; issues the day-to-day certificates.
profile.intermediate-ca.heading: Intermediate CA
profile.tls-server.help: HTTPS, mail or any service with a host name.
profile.tls-server.heading: TLS server certificate
profile.tls-client.help: A user or device that logs in with a certificate (mTLS, VPN, Wi-Fi).
profile.tls-client.heading: TLS client certificate
profile.smime.help: Sign and encrypt e-mail for one address.
profile.smime.heading: S/MIME certificate
profile.code-signing.help: Sign software, scripts or container images.
profile.code-signing.heading: Code signing certificate
profile.ssh.help: A login key; exported as authorized_keys line or PuTTY file.
profile.openpgp.help: A primary key with an encryption subkey, for GnuPG and mail.
profile.intro: Only what this purpose needs. Everything else follows from it and is listed on the right.
profile.hosts.help: One per line. IP addresses and *.wildcards work too. The first name becomes the certificate's name.
profile.email.help.smime: The address the certificate signs and encrypts for.
profile.noca: There is no CA with its private key yet.
profile.keytype: Key type of a new key
profile.keypass.help: Only for keys (or CA keys) with their own password.
profile.editor.help: Subject fields, extensions, the signature hash and dates: open the full editor; it keeps what you entered here.
profile.error.hosts: Enter at least one host name or IP address.
profile.error.country: The country is a two-letter code such as DE.
profile.error.issuer: Choose a CA that issues the certificate.
profile.error.key: Choose the key or the request.
summary.heading: What you will get
summary.name: Name
summary.key.new: new %s, protected by the database key
summary.warn.apple: Apple devices reject TLS server certificates valid for more than 825 days.
summary.warn.outlives: The certificate would outlive its CA, which expires on %s.
newsshkey.title: New SSH key
newsshkey.heading: New SSH key
newsshkey.help: Ed25519 is the usual choice; ECDSA and RSA are for systems that do not accept it. The comment is stored as the key's comment and written into its SSH files. The key is stored in the database, and the next page offers its files for OpenSSH and PuTTY.
sshkey.title: SSH key
sshkey.heading: SSH key
sshkey.public.help: This line goes into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server.
sshkey.nocomment: none, set it as the key's comment
sshkey.flavor.openssh.help: The private key in OpenSSH's format and the public key as an authorized_keys line, for ssh, ssh-agent and most other tools
sshkey.flavor.putty.help: The private key as a PPK file for PuTTY 0.75 and later, and the public key as PuTTYgen saves it (RFC 4716)
sshkey.flavor.putty2.help: As PuTTY, with a PPK version 2 file for older PuTTY versions, WinSCP and other tools that do not read version 3
sshkey.passphrase.help: With a passphrase the private key is encrypted; without one it is written unencrypted.
sshkey.error.notssh: This item is not a key that SSH can use.
newpgpkey.title: New OpenPGP key
newpgpkey.heading: New OpenPGP key
newpgpkey.help: Ed25519 with an X25519 encryption subkey is the usual choice. The primary key signs and certifies; the subkey encrypts. Both are stored as keys in the database, and the next page offers the key for GnuPG and other OpenPGP programs.
newpgpkey.error.input: Enter at least one user ID (one line each, at most 20) and choose the key type, version and expiry.
pgpkey.title: OpenPGP key
pgpkey.heading: OpenPGP key
pgpkey.subkeyof: This key is a subkey of the OpenPGP key
pgpkey.version.4: OpenPGP v4, for GnuPG and every other program
pgpkey.version.6: OpenPGP v6 (RFC 9580), for Sequoia, OpenPGP.js and gopenpgp; GnuPG cannot read it
pgpkey.uids.help: One per line, usually a name and an e-mail address in angle brackets. The first one is the primary user ID.
pgpkey.public.help: Give this block to others, or import it with gpg --import.
pgpkey.flavor.bundle.help: A ZIP archive with the public key, the secret key and a revocation certificate, all armored, as GnuPG keeps them
pgpkey.flavor.binary.help: The public key in binary form (.gpg), for keyrings and Web Key Directories
pgpkey.flavor.secret.help: The secret key with its subkeys, armored, for gpg --import
pgpkey.passphrase.help: With a passphrase the secret keys are encrypted; without one they are written unencrypted. The public key needs none.
pgpkey.addsubkey.help: A stored key, for example an SSH key as authentication subkey for gpg-agent, or a new encryption key. The subkey expires with the primary key.
pgpkey.subkey.name: %s (encryption)
pgpkey.remove.warn: The user IDs and signatures of this OpenPGP key are deleted; its keys stay in the database. Creating a certificate again gives the key a new fingerprint.
pgpkey.create.intro: Makes this key the primary key of an OpenPGP key with the user IDs below.
pgpkey.error.notpgp: This item is not a key that OpenPGP can use.
pgpkey.error.subkey: This key cannot be a subkey with this usage.
pgpkey.error.version: This key type exists only as a version 6 OpenPGP key.
pgpkey.error.noprivate: There is no private key for this OpenPGP key.
editor.reqsubject: Keep the subject of the request
editor.subject: Subject
editor.subjecthelp: When a request is selected and its subject is kept, these fields are ignored.
hash.auto: From the key (SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 by key size)
editor.keyhelp: A new key gets the internal name. Unused keys are listed first. The key password is only needed for keys with their own password. EdDSA, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and composite keys sign without a separate hash; RSA-PSS keys always sign with PSS.
renew.published.help: Checked, the renewal points to the issuer's CRL and certificate at the current base URLs, replacing earlier published URLs; other entries stay. Unchecked, the extension is copied as it is.
editor.published.help: The issuing CA's CRL and certificate as go-ca publishes them, below %s (all as mirrors). Self-signed certificates get neither. Further entries can be added below.
editor.syntaxhelp: Lists use OpenSSL syntax, separated by commas: DNS:, IP:, email:, URI:, RID:. DNS:copycn copies the common name, email:copy the e-mail address.
editor.error.keypass: A key with its own password is involved. Enter its password.
editor.error.mandatory: The mandatory subject entry %s is empty.
item.notice.revoked: The certificate was revoked. It appears on the next CRL.
ca.error.revoke: The certificate could not be revoked. Details are in the server log.
ca.error.properties: Invalid CA properties: the CRL interval must be between 1 and 36500 days.
ca.autocrl.on: on: signed after every revocation change and after half of the CRL interval
ca.autocrl.nobg: off: this database is not kept open in the background; sign CRLs by hand
ca.autocrl.ownpass: off: the CA key has its own password; sign CRLs by hand
ca.autocrl.nokey: off: the CA's private key is not in the database
item.notice.crlsigned: A new CRL was signed and published.
item.error.crl: The CRL could not be signed.
item.error.ratelimit: Too many failed attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
rev.title: Revocations
rev.heading: Revocations of %s
rev.help: Only certificates this CA issued that are in the database (also in the trash) can be revoked. A revocation stays on the CRL until 30 days after the certificate expired, even once the certificate is deleted. Editing keeps the revocation date. Leave the date empty for no invalidity date.
rev.error.input: The revocation could not be saved: check the serial number and the date.
rev.error.unknown: No certificate with this serial number from this CA is in the database.
rev.status.unknown: not on the CRL: certificate unknown
rev.status.aged: not on the CRL: expired more than 30 days ago
crlgen.title: Generate CRL
crlgen.heading: Generate a CRL for %s

crlgen.count.zero: No certificates are revoked; the CRL will be empty.
crlgen.count.one: %d revocation will be on the CRL.
crlgen.count.other: %d revocations will be on the CRL.

crlgen.issueralt: Issuer alternative name (copy of the CA's subject alternative name)
crlgen.error.input: The CRL could not be generated: check the dates and the CRL number.
renew.title: Renew certificate
renew.heading: Renew %s
renew.help: The new certificate keeps subject, key and extensions and is signed by the same issuer. A renewed CA takes over the certificates and revocations of the old one.
renew.error.input: The certificate could not be renewed: check the dates.
editor.apply.subject: Apply subject
editor.start.help: A purpose sets key type, validity and extensions and keeps the subject; a template also brings its subject. Folded sections show their values; open them to change.
editor.netscape.help: Only for very old clients; current browsers and libraries ignore them.
editor.expert.used: Hidden expert fields hold values: %s. They are kept; show expert fields to see or change them.
editor.templatesubject: Subject entries left empty are not part of the template.
editor.advancedhelp: Further extensions in OpenSSL configuration syntax, one per line, e.g. certificatePolicies, policyConstraints or OID = DER:…; sections like [alt] can be referenced with @alt. Unknown lines are reported, not ignored.
item.error.totemplate: The template could not be created. Details are in the server log.
oid.title: OID resolver
oid.heading: OID resolver
oid.help: Searches the object identifiers go-ca knows, including XCA's own additions. Names match in part.

export.heading: Export
export.comment: Include the internal name and comment in PEM files
export.password.help: Only used by encrypted formats (PKCS#12, PKCS#8 encrypted, PEM encrypted).
export.show.help: Text formats can be shown here and copied to the clipboard.
export.error.selection: Nothing to export: select items of one type.
export.error.nopassword: This format encrypts the private key: enter an export password.

fmt.help.cert_jwk_chain: The public key of the certificate in JSON Web Key format with X.509 certificate thumbprint (x5t) and certificate chain (x5c)

fmt.help.key_pem_private: Unencrypted private key in text format
fmt.help.key_pem_encrypted: OpenSSL's traditional encrypted private key in text format. Its password is turned into a key with a single MD5 round, which is cheap to attack; prefer PKCS #8 encrypted unless old software needs this format
fmt.help.key_ssh2_public: The public key encoded in SSH2 format
fmt.help.key_openssh_private: Unencrypted private key in OpenSSH's own format with the key comment, as ssh-keygen writes it
fmt.help.key_openssh_encrypted: Private key in OpenSSH's own format with the key comment, protected by a passphrase (bcrypt, AES-256)
fmt.help.key_ppk: Unencrypted private key for PuTTY 0.75 and later (PPK version 3)
fmt.help.key_ppk_encrypted: Private key for PuTTY 0.75 and later (PPK version 3), protected by a passphrase (Argon2id, AES-256)
fmt.help.key_ppk2: Unencrypted private key for older PuTTY versions, WinSCP and other tools that do not read version 3 (PPK version 2)
fmt.help.key_ppk2_encrypted: Private key for older PuTTY versions, WinSCP and other tools that do not read version 3 (PPK version 2), protected by a passphrase
fmt.help.key_rfc4716_public: The public key as an RFC 4716 block, the format PuTTYgen saves public keys in
fmt.help.key_pgp_public: The OpenPGP public key with its user IDs and subkeys, armored, for gpg --import
fmt.help.key_pgp_public_binary: The OpenPGP public key in binary form
fmt.help.key_pgp_secret: The OpenPGP secret key with its subkeys, armored and unencrypted
fmt.help.key_pgp_secret_encrypted: The OpenPGP secret key with its subkeys, armored and encrypted with a passphrase
fmt.help.key_pgp_revocation: A revocation certificate signed by the primary key; importing it revokes the OpenPGP key
fmt.help.key_der_public: Binary DER format of the public key
fmt.help.key_der_private: Unencrypted private key in binary DER format
fmt.help.key_pvk: Private key in Microsoft PVK format, not encrypted. Only for old Microsoft tools such as signtool with pvk2pfx
fmt.help.key_pkcs8_encrypted: Encrypted private key in PKCS#8 text format
fmt.help.key_pkcs8: Unencrypted private key in PKCS#8 text format
fmt.help.key_jwk_private: Unencrypted private key in JSON Web Key format
fmt.help.key_jwk_public: Public key in JSON Web Key format
fmt.help.req_der: Binary DER format of the certificate request
fmt.help.crl_der: Binary DER format of the revocation list
fmt.help.crl_vcal: vCalendar reminder for the CRL expiry date

fmt.help.tmpl_multi: All selected XCA templates in PEM-like format. Templates include the internal name and comment

importitems.title: Import
importitems.heading: Import items
importitems.files: Files (PEM, DER, PKCS#7, PKCS#8, PKCS#12, OpenSSH, PuTTY, PVK, CRL, XCA templates)
importitems.paste: Or paste PEM, SSH or PuTTY text
importitems.help: Everything found is listed for review before anything is stored. Up to %d MB in total.
importitems.error.nofile: Choose a file or paste PEM text.
importitems.error.failed: The import failed. See the server log.
import.key_extended: Extending public key from %s by imported key '%s'
dump.heading: Dump database
dump.help: Download every item as PEM files in a ZIP archive, in folders like XCA's "Dump database". Private keys are encrypted with the password you enter here. Keys with their own password are included only if they are stored as standard encrypted PKCS#8; the others are listed in keys/OWN-PASSWORD.txt with their public key.
dh.title: DH parameters
dh.heading: Diffie-Hellman parameters
dh.intro: Diffie-Hellman parameters are needed by different applications (for example OpenVPN), but not stored in the database. They are generated in the background and offered as a PEM download.
dh.timing: 1024 to 4096 bits. 2048 bits usually take seconds, 4096 bits can take many minutes.
dh.running: Generating %s bit parameters for %s, %d candidates tested…
dh.error.bits: Enter a size from 1024 to 4096 bits.
importitems.duplicate: Found more than once in this import
login.error.busy: Too many sign-ins at the same moment. Try again in a few seconds.
create.error.short: The password must have at least 8 characters.
converting.title: Converting the database
converting.heading: Converting the database
converting.intro: This XCA database is imported into a new go-ca database. Its private keys are re-encrypted with a new data key, which your password protects through Argon2id. When the new database is verified, the .xdb file is deleted. This happens once; the database opens when it is done.
converted.ownpass: The database was imported. %s keys need their own password and keep XCA's encryption until that password is entered the next time; then they are re-encrypted too.
dbpw.keep: Leave the new password empty to keep the current one, for example to change only the key derivation cost. At least %d characters.
dbpw.kdf.heading: Key derivation (Argon2id)
dbpw.kdf.help: Memory and passes make each guess at the password expensive. They are spent once per login. The default is %d MiB with %d passes; lower them only for small devices.
dbpw.error.kdf: Choose one of the offered key derivation settings.
dbpw.error.short: The new password must have at least %s characters.
dump.error.password: Enter the same password for the private keys twice.

list.legacy.one: %d key with its own password is still encrypted as XCA stored it. Check it once with its password to re-encrypt it with go-ca's encryption.
list.legacy.other: %d keys with their own password are still encrypted as XCA stored them. Check each once with its password to re-encrypt it with go-ca's encryption.

converted.done: %s was imported into this go-ca database and then deleted.
opt.crl_days_root: CRL interval of new root CAs (days)
opt.crl_days_sub: CRL interval of new subordinate CAs (days)
opt.backup_days: Delete backups older than (days, 0 = never; the newest backup always stays)
trash.title: Trash
trash.heading: Trash
trash.intro: Deleted items stay here until they are deleted for good. Restoring an item links it again to its certificates, keys and issuer. Private keys in the trash stay encrypted.
trash.purge.confirm: Yes, delete for good; this cannot be undone
trash.empty.warn: Every item in the trash is deleted for good, private keys included, and the database file is rebuilt so that nothing of them remains. Backups still contain them.
trash.error: That did not work; the item may have changed in the meantime.
trash.error.authority: This CA certificate cannot be restored: it was renewed, and the renewed CA certificate now holds its authority ID, folder and issued certificates. Move the renewed one to the trash first.
audit.title: Log
audit.heading: Log
audit.intro: Everything that changed this database, and every export of a private key. Entries cannot be changed or deleted. Passwords and keys are never logged.
audit.action.key.password_reset: Key password reset to the database password
